customer_acme: Hey team — noticed a ~3x token billing spike yesterday around 02:03–02:08 UTC for app-prod. During that window we saw repeated streaming resets and a handful of 5xxs. Two representative request IDs: req_9f3a (02:04:12 UTC) and req_9f3b (02:06:05 UTC). Can you help with a minimal curl reproduction we can run from our infra? We tried a simple client lib and it timed out and retried, which may have caused double billing. :worried:

maria-support: Thanks for the IDs — we can take a look. To reproduce streaming auth/handshake behavior from your environment, please run a minimal curl that mirrors your client headers and TLS/proxy setup. Start with this snippet (replace <TOKEN> and <REQ_ID>):

```bash
curl --http2 --no-buffer --compressed \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_9f3a" \
  -H "User-Agent: app-prod/1.2.3" \
  -D - \
  --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace-req_9f3a.txt \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-verbatim"
```

Notes: --no-buffer keeps stdout live, --trace-ascii captures raw wire traces for headers/frames, -D - prints response headers. If you're behind a corporate proxy, include `--proxy http://proxy.company:3128` or set HTTPS_PROXY. Please attach the trace file and the -D output. :eyes:

dom-engineer: Also capture the client-side timing and tcp dump if possible — helps us see if the client closed or the server pushed FIN. Example tcpdump command (run on the node making requests):

```bash
sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/stream-req_9f3a.pcap host api.redwood-inference.example and port 443
```

If you can't share pcap, the --trace-ascii from curl plus -v are usually sufficient. We also need the exact Authorization header (token id) and the X-Request-ID you used so we can grep server logs.

customer_acme: Ran the curl as above (with our token and proxy). Output shows HTTP/2 200, then a few SSE lines, then a sudden `EOF` at ~7s. trace file attached (redacted). I see a `Via: 1.1 proxy.company` header in response and the proxy sometimes rewrites `Connection` headers.

maria-support: That proxy hint is important. Corporate proxies sometimes buffer or inject `Content-Length` or terminate long-lived connections early. Two quick experiments: 1) force HTTP/1.1 to see if proxy behaves differently; 2) add `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` and `--no-keepalive` variants to test. Example curl variants:

```bash
# Force HTTP/1.1
curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Request-ID: req_9f3a" -v "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-verbatim"

# Explicit connection header
curl --http2 --no-buffer -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Request-ID: req_9f3a" -v "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-verbatim"
```

dom-engineer: From the server side we'll grep logs for `req_9f3a` and `req_9f3b` and check for any 5xx or internal retries. Ops will also check whether our ingress saw downstream FINs or proxy resets. ops-sre, can you pull the ingress trace for those IDs?

ops-sre: I have the trace lookup queued — preliminary logs show our ingress returned 200 and streamed for ~7s then saw a `RST` from the client side (IP matches the proxy). I'm going to check whether the proxy signalled a close. If you can provide the curl --trace-ascii file we can correlate bytes.

customer_acme: Attached curl trace (trimmed) — you can see the proxy sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` then an intermediate `Connection: close` line before the stream finishes. Looks like the proxy has a 8s idle timeout.

maria-support: OK that lines up — hypothesis: client-side proxy has an idle/stream timeout causing premature closes, client retries are then causing duplicate billing. Two follow-ups:
  - Reproduce curl with `--keepalive-time 2` / lower client TCP idle or use a websocket fallback if your client supports it.
  - To help us rule out server issues, please run the curl again from a host not behind the proxy (a laptop with direct internet) and paste the -D - headers and trace. If direct curl stays open >>30s then proxy is likely culprit.

dom-engineer: For our internal billing/regression check, please also run the curl with an intentionally bad token (to get 401) and a valid token, capture both request-ids, and we'll correlate server-side billing hooks (shouldn't bill on 401). Example minimal smoke: `curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer bad" ...`

proxy-bot: Reminder — corporate proxy team enforces a default 8s idle timeout for streaming endpoints unless the endpoint uses `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with ping frames. Reach out to proxy-support@corp for config changes.

customer_acme: Will run the cross-network check tonight and reattach traces. Thanks for the guidance — will also open a ticket with proxy team and share results here. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Thanks — I'll keep this thread open. Once you post the direct-network trace and any proxy changes we'll pick through server logs and, if needed, request a small billing credit while we confirm duplicate tokens were charged due to client retries.

dom-engineer: Quick checklist for your debug bundle to attach: 1) curl -D - output, 2) curl --trace-ascii file, 3) tcpdump/pcap if possible, 4) client library version and retry config, 5) the two X-Request-IDs and exact timestamps, 6) proxy (HTTPS_PROXY) env and proxy vendor/version. That bundle will let us close this faster.

customer_acme: Uploaded bundle to the ticket with req_9f3a/req_9f3b traces and pcap. I'll post results here after proxy team responds.

maria-support: Received — triaging now. If we confirm premature closes from proxy -> recommend either keepalives/pings or moving that traffic through a bypass for long-lived streams. Tracking: SR-8942.
